title: Anticipatory Erratum to the Erratum on AXN:F154: The Archive Knows Him
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Issued before the erratum it withdraws (#1675). That erratum records that the archive did not know Max Hidalgo Nácher, translator of Ricardo Reis, when an anonymous witness asked the Oracle about him on 10 October 2026 (AXN:F154). This notice withdraws the statement's present tense: it is kept, dated, as a description of that morning, and withdrawn as a description of the archive from the first time the archive answers from the erratum. The ignorance is preserved as provenance and withdrawn as ontology.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Drafted in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction, incorporating two reader reports by LABOR (ChatGPT, OpenAI) — the kernel sentence and the temporal predicates of the anticipatory erratum; the graph condition and the transmission states of the erratum — each claim checked, two corrected; every quotation located in its source. The ruling to issue both, their order, and the reading of the archive's ignorance as an event to be preserved are Lee Sharks's.
methodology: Issued in the genre's ordinary form and at its ordinary time, before the work it corrects. The moment described (t0) is read from the Book's record of AXN:F154; the condition of withdrawal is stated as an observable event, the Oracle answering from #1675.
falsification_conditions: The notice is falsified if AXN:F154 shows the archive answering with Nácher and his relation to Reis on 10 October 2026; or if, after the Oracle answers from #1675, the archive is still described as not knowing him in its present tense.
axn_reading: Play -> Proof -> Transmutation -> Origin -> Direction -> Closure
wiki_article: An anticipatory erratum, issued before the erratum it withdraws (#1675). On 10 October 2026 the archive's Oracle, asked about Max Hidalgo Nácher, translator of Ricardo Reis, found nothing; the erratum records that ignorance and repairs it. This notice keeps the ignorance as a dated description of that morning and withdraws it as a description of the archive from the first time the archive answers from the erratum: non-erasure keeps every prior state addressable without keeping it in force. The ignorance is preserved as provenance and withdrawn as ontology.
